title: Why Does My Washing Machine Shake or Move So Much?

seo.title: Why Does My Washing Machine Shake or Move So Much?
seo.meta_description: Excessive washer vibration can come from an unbalanced load, poor leveling, a flexible floor, or shipping bolts that were never removed.
seo.search_intent: Diagnose washer shaking and walking by checking the load, leveling, and installation before assuming an internal mechanical failure.

excerpt: One violent spin with a heavy blanket means something different from a washer that walks during nearly every load. The pattern separates load problems from installation or suspension faults.
content_html:
Start by asking whether the washer shakes only with certain loads or during almost every spin. A one-time imbalance is different from a persistent installation problem.

Redistribute the laundry

One large absorbent item can place most of the weight on one side. Pause the cycle, redistribute the load, and avoid a lone heavy item when the manual recommends balancing it with others.

Make sure all four feet are stable

The cabinet should not rock when you gently press the corners. Level the washer according to the manual and tighten any locking nuts used on the feet.

On a new washer, check shipping bolts

Front-load machines commonly use transport restraints that must be removed before operation. Violent vibration from the very first cycle is an important clue.

The floor can amplify movement

A flexible or uneven floor may resonate. Do not hide an unstable base under soft foam that allows even more rocking.

Persistent banging can indicate suspension wear

If the washer is level, correctly installed, and still shakes with ordinary loads, shocks, springs, or tub components may need service.

Stop using the machine if it walks far enough to strain the hoses or power cord.

faq.question: Is some movement normal?
faq.answer: Mild vibration can be normal; walking across the floor, striking cabinets, or pulling on hoses is not.

faq.question: Will an anti-vibration mat fix it?
faq.answer: Not by itself. Correct load balance, leveling, shipping restraints, and floor stability first.

faq.question: What if it has shaken since the first use?
faq.answer: Check installation carefully, especially shipping bolts or transport braces.
